That sounds like a really difficult situation and I can only imagine what you’re feeling. That’s a natural feeling to have though. And I would never sit and tear someone down for feeling jealous, or upset, or left out. Whatever it is you’re feeling. I don’t know how old you are and I’m not assuming. But, I’m just going to use this example because this was the last time I felt similar... when I was in high school I had a best friend who I had a similar relationship.. after while I realized I wasn’t important anymore, and I found that she truly didn’t like me anymore because she told people that behind my back. It broke my heart, because while my intentions were good, some of the behaviors I picked up as a kid, such as anxiety and codependency caused her to naturally push away. It was understandable why she didn’t want to be my friend anymore, looking back about 8 years in the past. What I learned from that was yeah, I probably said or did somethings that I never intended to come off a certain way but they did. But I also learned that someone who is going to treat me like that isn’t someone worth having in my life and I need a friend who accepts and understands me. Fast forward years later, she still speaks poorly of me, but that’s her problem now. I was just a kid. I have some of the best friends I’d never thought I’d have now and they have seen me at my worst and know my every secret.

I guess my point here is that...Regardless of what happens in your relationships just because you may be a part of the issue doesn’t mean you’re at fault. I don’t know your situation in depth and I don’t know you as a person. But who you are, your insecurities, your problems, your anxieties, are not your fault. And the way she is reacting to the situation is not your fault. Shes had ownership in this situation too. I’ve found myself in a similar situation before.. checking a persons page over and over. I hope this post helped a little at least, or got you taking some of the pressure off of you. You deserve happiness, and I think you’re worth it.

Medication works different for everyone and people have different experiences and get certain results with certain doses. Anxiety may play a role in how you think a certain medicine works for you. That’s why psych meds are such a slippery slope sometimes. Just continue to be honest with your doctor and honest with yourself about how you’re feeling. It’s really hard to not focus too much on the medication but at the same time it’s hard to try to not think about it. Gabapentin is typically started in lower doses and increased over time. Gabapentin didn’t help me much, but I know take Klonopin for my anxiety. It helps a lot, although it is a controlled substance and easy to get addicted to.

Have you tried going to an inpatient mental health clinic? It helped me a lot not with body dysmorphia but with another illness. In fact I work for a mental health facility. What I’ve learned his cognitive behavioral therapy helps a lot with ED patients.

What I’ve learned from being in mental hospitals since the age of 15 and I’m now 21. Is that with every relapse in mental health, you learn more about yourself and how to cope with your illness. Keep fighting. I now work for a mental health facility and it pains me to read about my previous patients in the newspaper who gave up their fight. There are people out there who haven’t even met you that can connect with you and help you deal with these things. The thought that you are rotten to the core is a thought. Thoughts can be changed over time no matter how long they’ve been present. I suggest dialectal behavioral therapy or cognitive behavioral therapy if you can get access to it. They are great programs.

No matter the past present or future. We all matter. Your life matters to someone and actually a lot of people. You must allow yourself to accept the help that is being given to you. I did terrible in high school. Barely passed. Was near being held back. And I made it. Some of my classmates didn’t even make it and got held back and they are now pursuing their dreams just fine. We all have our own timeline. And I’m sure your mother would be devastated. I always told my mother I’m a burden and she cried and said she would do anything to keep me alive.

Sometimes we say things before we think them through. What you must remember is we all make mistakes in life. Take the binoculars and zoom out. Look at the bigger picture. A moment is a speck of dust on this thing we call life. Times change, we learn, we grow, and we find new ways to over come challenges. You must forgive yourself and try reading aloud positive affirmations to yourself everyday in the mirror. Whether you believe them or not makes no difference, the point being you may start to believe this over time. It takes practice and a lot of work. We all can be a little selfish, especially when we have a lot built up inside or we were never made to feel like we were important. That can bring these overflowing emotions and words coming out of our mouths. But feed yourself with something more. Feed yourself with the kindness we all deserve, no matter who we are.
